definition: careful thought; or something given in exchange
memoryTip: Careful thought — or the thing given in a deal (legal sense).
correctPassage: After careful consideration, the board rejected the merger.
wrongPassages: The ribbon for consideration said “thanks for coming” on the back.
She painted the drum “consideration” and stored last year’s festival maps.
In the kitchen, a consideration pinch of salt weighed exactly one gram on the scale.

definition: marked by decline or luxurious self-indulgence
memoryTip: De-cadence: falling from standards — luxuriously self-indulgent decline.
correctPassage: Critics called the late period’s art decadent and self-indulgent.
wrongPassages: Parents described the toddler’s decadent tantrum as calm, quiet, and brief.
The plan was decadent because every risk had already been eliminated.
A decadent workout meant water only and lights out by nine.

correctPassage: Rising seas have imperiled several coastal archaeological sites.
wrongPassages: They imperiled the experiment by powering down and leaving for lunch.
She hoped to imperiled the debt by charging more interest on the same balance.
The crisis was imperiled the moment it started: already fully resolved.

memoryTip: Like a charming rogue — mischievous, not fully serious.
correctPassage: A roguish smile suggested he was not entirely serious.
wrongPassages: Judges called the ruling roguish because it carefully weighed both sides.
His roguish explanation listed steps 1–5 with diagrams for every term.
The software will roguish your password by turning each character into an emoji.

definition: relating to a roguish hero’s episodic adventures
memoryTip: Picaro = rogue hero — a rascal’s string of misadventures.
correctPassage: The novel is picaresque: a clever outsider stumbles through one episode after another.
wrongPassages: The fuse rating was picaresque and never protected the circuit it named.
She filed the forms under “picaresque” as if it were a department code.
The snow shelf felt picaresque after a deck and railing were installed.

definition: change direction when passing through a medium
memoryTip: Re-fract light: bend it as it passes through glass or water.
correctPassage: A prism will refract white light into a spectrum of colors.
wrongPassages: To refract the budget, accountants printed extra copies and stacked them.
They hoped to refract attendance by cancelling the event and locking the doors.
Please refract the window before you leave so the rain does not get in.

definition: standard or commonly used; not original
memoryTip: Off-the-shelf stock answer — standard, not original.
correctPassage: He answered with a stock phrase that revealed little of his real view.
wrongPassages: Her stock response listed original research no one else had attempted.
Critics praised the stock ending for inventing a form never seen before.
His stock proposal was so original that no template or precedent applied.

definition: a sudden invasion or raid into territory
memoryTip: In + course/run — a sudden run into someone else’s ground.
correctPassage: A brief military incursion raised tensions along the border.
wrongPassages: She used “incursion” as a filename for an empty desktop document.
He retagged the orphan keys “incursion” and still could not match a lock.
The recipe called for one incursion of flour, which meant “about a cup.”

definition: give or enhance the value or status of
memoryTip: Valor + ize — assign value or raise the status of something.
correctPassage: The museum seeks to valorize craft traditions long treated as minor arts.
wrongPassages: They tried to valorize the stain with the solvent that set it permanently.
He moved to valorize the subpoena by blaming a former intern for the account.
To valorize the experiment, the team powered down and left for lunch.

memoryTip: Originally kill every tenth; now destroy a large share.
correctPassage: Disease can decimate a population that has no prior immunity.
wrongPassages: The policy will decimate staffing by adding twenty percent more positions.
Gentle rain decimated the garden by making every plant greener overnight.
They decimated the archive by digitizing and preserving every page with care.
